posts.title: How to ask a Missouri court for the Driver Improvement Program, and what the 60-day clock means
posts.description: Missouri courts can let you complete an 8-hour Driver Improvement Program so the points for a ticket are never assessed. You have to ask, you have 60 days from your plea, and you can do it once every 36 months. Here is how.

faq.q: Who authorizes the Missouri Driver Improvement Program?
faq.a: The court handling your ticket, or the Fine Collection Center if the ticket was sent there. The Department of Revenue does not authorize it; it records the completion.

faq.q: How long do I have to finish DIP?
faq.a: Sixty days from your guilty plea or conviction.

faq.q: How often can I use DIP?

sources.name: Missouri Department of Revenue — Tickets and Points FAQ
Missouri Safety Center — Driver Improvement Program

posts.content:
**Short answer:** Ask the court handling your ticket, or the Fine Collection Center, whether you may complete an approved Driver Improvement Program. If the answer is yes, finish an eight-hour approved program within 60 days of your guilty plea, and the points for that violation are not assessed on your record. The conviction still records. You can do this once every 36 months.

## Who decides

The court. The Department of Revenue's own guidance says that "in certain cases, the court or the Fine Collections Center may authorize you to complete a Driver Improvement Program." No provider, and no amount of enrolling early, substitutes for that authorization. Ask first.

## How to ask

1. **Find where your ticket is.** Municipal court, circuit court, or the statewide Fine Collection Center. It is printed on the citation.
2. **Contact the clerk** before your court date or before you pay, and ask whether you may complete a Driver Improvement Program in lieu of points. Some courts have a form; some handle it at the appearance; some prosecutors offer it as part of a plea.
3. **Get the authorization in writing** if you can, and note the date of your plea or conviction. Your 60 days run from that date.
4. **Enroll the same day** in an approved program. The Missouri Safety Center approves programs; [ours](/missouri) is eight hours, $24.99, online.

## The 60-day clock

Missouri requires the program to be completed within 60 days of the plea or conviction. The course is eight hours and the paperwork is one form, so 60 days is comfortable if you start in the first week and tight if you start in the seventh. Most people finish across three or four evenings.

## After you finish

You receive a certificate and a completion form. The DOR's guidance is that "you or the program may mail the completion form" to the Missouri Department of Revenue, Driver License Bureau, PO Box 200, Jefferson City, MO 65105-0200. Mail it promptly, keep proof, and give the court a copy if it asked for one.

## What DIP does and does not do

- **Does:** stops the points for this violation from being assessed on your record.
- **Does not:** remove the conviction, refund the fine, or remove points already on your record from earlier tickets. Those fall off on their own: a third after one year without a new conviction, half after two, all after three.

## Once every 36 months

Use it wisely. If you have used DIP to avoid points in the past three years, the court cannot authorize it again yet.

posts.title: Missouri points: what 4, 8 and 12 points do to your license
posts.description: Four points in 12 months is a warning letter. Eight in 18 months is a 30-day suspension. Twelve in 12 months is a one-year revocation. Here is Missouri's point system, how points fall off, and how the Driver Improvement Program fits.

faq.q: How many points suspends a Missouri license?
faq.a: Eight or more points in 18 months brings a 30-day suspension for a first suspension, 60 days for a second and 90 days for a third.

faq.q: How many points revokes a Missouri license?
faq.a: Twelve or more points in 12 months, 18 or more in 24 months, or 24 or more in 36 months brings a one-year revocation.

faq.q: How do Missouri points come off?
faq.a: By a third after one year with no new conviction, by half after two years, and entirely after three years.

sources.name: Missouri Department of Revenue — Tickets and Points FAQ

posts.content:
**Short answer:** Missouri assigns points to moving-violation convictions under RSMo 302.302. Four points in 12 months earns a warning letter. Eight points in 18 months is a 30-day suspension (60 days for a second, 90 for a third). Twelve points in 12 months, 18 in 24, or 24 in 36 is a one-year revocation. Points fall off on their own over three years, and a court-authorized Driver Improvement Program keeps the points from a new violation off entirely.

## Common point values

Most moving violations are two points when the conviction is in a municipal court and three points in state court, with higher values for the serious offenses: driving while intoxicated, driving while suspended or revoked, and leaving the scene carry eight to twelve points. Speeding is generally two or three points depending on the court. Check the DOR's schedule for the exact figure on your conviction.

## The three thresholds

| Points | Window | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | 12 months | Warning letter |
| 8 | 18 months | Suspension: 30 days (first), 60 (second), 90 (third) |
| 12 / 18 / 24 | 12 / 24 / 36 months | Revocation for one year |

## How points come off

Every year you go without a new conviction, your total is reduced: by one third after the first year, by half of what remains after the second, and to zero after the third.

## Where the Driver Improvement Program fits

DIP does not remove points already on your record. It stops the points from a **new** violation being assessed, when the court or the Fine Collection Center authorizes it and you finish an approved eight-hour program within 60 days of your plea. Once every 36 months. If you are at six points with a new ticket pending, that is the difference between a warning and a suspension. We wrote up [how to ask the court](/missouri/blog/how-to-ask-missouri-court-for-driver-improvement-program), and [our program](/missouri) is $24.99.

## What to do today

1. Request your driver record from the DOR and count the points inside the last 12 and 18 months.
2. If a new ticket is pending, ask the court about DIP before you plead.
3. If you are already suspended or revoked, read your notice: reinstatement has its own steps, and DIP is not one of them.
